To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a cable-driven mechanism for a miniature three-fingered manipulator that is suitable for minimally invasive surgery and that can be actuated by a master robot.

the cable-driven mechanism can be designed in such a way that the instrument is able to perform the same tasks as a human hand, that the mechanism is miniaturized and that it has a human-centered appearance, which is a prerequisite for acceptance of a robot-assisted system.
the design of the mechanism and its cable routing of the instrument are based on the human hand, and that its input-output functions are derived by a novel method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a miniature serial multi-DOF manipulator for robot assisted minimally invasive surgery.
the design of a cable-driven miniature serial manipulator, which will be the basis for the design of the slave instrument of a master-slave surgical robot system.
a novel cable-driven design of a miniature three-fingered robotic hand that is capable of grasping and performing dexterous manipulation tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a multi-DOFs cable-driven mechanism can be designed to meet the requirements of a miniature serial robot for minimally invasive surgery.
the design of such a miniature multi-DOF manipulator is possible and that the presented design is a promising solution for a teleoperated robot for minimally invasive surgery.

the proposed design is suitable for the application of a miniature multi-fingered hand as a slave instrument for robot-assisted surgery and that the proposed methods are suitable for deriving the input-output relations of its cable-driven mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method can be applied to any mechanism with a similar design and the derived equations can be used in the simulation of the mechanism.
we have developed a miniature three-fingered hand with three independent DOFs for each of the three fingers.
the design of the instrument was completed, its kinematic and static analysis was carried out, and its prototype was manufactured.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism can be designed such that the input-output functions are independent of the cable routing.
the design of such a mechanism is possible and the method of designing it is applicable to other cable-driven mechanisms.
the design of the mechanism is a trade-off between the number of active joints and the number of cables.
